title: Biovanta POC scoping - open model shortlist
next_steps: Redwood to share pricing and Dedicated capacity options and pilot contract
Customer to send 5k sample dataset + success criteria doc
SE to run baseline benchmark on provided dataset and share results (p50/p95 latency, tokens, throughput)
Schedule 1-hour technical deep-dive on on-prem/VPC networking and KMS integration
action_items: Ethan Kim (Redwood): share benchmark runner, scripts and sample infra templates; due: 2027-01-22
Dr. Lena Ortiz (Biovanta): deliver 5k sample dataset and written success criteria (latency, accuracy targets, languages); due: 2027-01-21
Sofia Patel (Redwood AE): send pricing deck, pilot SOW and security pack (SOC2/ISO docs); due: 2027-01-24
Markus Chen (Biovanta): confirm concurrency targets and existing K8s/VPC details; due: 2027-01-25
summary: POC scoping focused on open-model shortlist for a Biovanta therapeutics use case (clinical note summarization + multilingual support). Discussed success criteria (factuality, hallucination tolerance, latency), workload sizing (concurrent users, tokens), benchmark plan and 6-week timeline. Redwood recommended initial shortlist (Mistral-7B, Llama-3-13B, Falcon-40B-instruct, MPT-30B) with tradeoffs on latency vs accuracy and quantization options. Agreed next steps: customer to provide sample dataset and success criteria; Redwood to run baseline benchmarks and share pricing/security docs.
topics: POC success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark metrics (latency, throughput, quality); open-model shortlist; quantization/encoding and inference config; dedicated vs hosted tradeoff; security/KMS/VPC; timeline and next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: alright everyone, thanks for joining. this is Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account. Ethan from our SE team is with me. quick roll call?
[00:07] Dr. Lena Ortiz: hey, lena here, head of ML at Biovanta. we have Markus and priya, and aisha on the call.
[00:13] Markus Chen: yep, marked, platform eng.
[00:15] Priya Singh: priya, data privacy.
[00:17] Aisha Rahman: aisha, nlp engineer.
[00:20] Ethan Kim: great. objective for today: scope the POC, align on success criteria, sizing, and pick an open-model shortlist that balances quality and latency for your clinical summarization + multilingual needs.
[00:33] Dr. Lena Ortiz: perfect. high level — our aim is to summarize clinician notes into structured patient summaries for downstream analytics, and also support spanish and french input. accuracy/factuality is the top priority, hallucination minimization. latency needs to be... reasonable, p50 ideally under 400ms for 256 token outputs, p95 under 1s if possible.
[00:54] Ethan Kim: noted. can you tell us expected traffic? qps, concurrency, avg tokens per request?
[00:58] Dr. Lena Ortiz: average 600 tokens input, 200 token output. peak concurrency around 30-40 concurrent inference requests during batch processing windows; burst up to 100 during reprocessing. daily active users small, but background jobs heavy.
[01:15] Sofia Patel: okay so mixed interactive + batch. that pushes us to think about batching for cost savings but also keeping interactive latency tight. what are your privacy constraints?
[01:23] Priya Singh: data must remain in our VPC and encrypted at rest, we need KMS integration, audit logs and retention policies. SOC2 is required, and we'll need to review redwood's security docs, plus potential on-prem option for an air-gapped env for PHI.
[01:38] Ethan Kim: totally expected. Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) supports KMS and audit logs, we can outline options. for POC we often do hosted with encrypted transport + enterprise agreements, or a private VPC staging cluster. depends on your legal comfort.
[01:52] Aisha Rahman: on model side, our engineers worry about specialized biomedical terminology — abbreviations and lab values. do we need domain-finetuned models or can instruction-tuned open models suffice?
[02:02] Ethan Kim: short answer: depends on quality bar. models like Llama-3-13B and Falcon-40B-instruct show strong general instruction-following; Mistral-7B is cost-efficient. For biomedical accuracy you might want a light domain adapt (LoRA) or prompt engineering + retrieval/KB to reduce hallucinations.
[02:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: we prefer minimal fine-tuning initially — faster POC. retrieval augmentation is okay if it keeps latency acceptable.
[02:25] Sofia Patel: good. i'll propose a shortlist for the initial run: Mistral-7B (fast, cost-efficient), LLaMA-3-13B (higher quality, larger), Falcon-40B-instruct (strong instruction tuning), MPT-30B (balanced). we can test quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) to see perf/quality tradeoffs.
[02:41] Markus Chen: can you run benchmarks with and without quantization? and measure p50/p95 latency and throughput?
[02:47] Ethan Kim: yes, we'll run baseline for each model on your sample dataset with: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE for summaries plus human spot checks for hallucination). we'll also provide cost estimates per 1M tokens.
[03:05] Priya Singh: who will run that? our infra or redwood?
[03:08] Ethan Kim: preferred: you send sample data and an anonymized set, we run in our infra to produce apples-to-apples numbers; if you need on-prem numbers we can provide runner scripts for you to run internally.
[03:20] Aisha Rahman: on multilingual — spanish and french primarily; occasional japanese. which models have good multilingual capabilities?
[03:26] Ethan Kim: LLaMA-3 has decent multilingual; Mistral less so but still serviceable; Falcon's larger variants have multilingual coverage but size increases cost. recommendation: include a multilingual-focused evaluation slice and if needed fallback to a specialized multilingual model or use an ensemble approach.
[03:44] Dr. Lena Ortiz: timeline — what's a realistic POC length? we were thinking 4-6 weeks.
[03:48] Sofia Patel: 6 weeks is realistic: week 0-1: setup + infra and security sign-off; week 2: baseline runs on 2-3 models; week 3-4: quality evaluation + adjustments (quantization, prompts, retrieval); week 5: extended load testing and latency tuning; week 6: final report + exec demo.
[04:06] Markus Chen: any risk of models failing compliance because of data exposure in hosted runs?
[04:10] Priya Singh: yes, that's our concern — PHI.
[04:12] Ethan Kim: we can map that out: hosted with contractual data controls and encryption, or private VPC where data never leaves your network. for PHI we recommend private deployment or dedicated capacity at minimum.
[04:24] Sofia Patel: cost tradeoffs — dedicated vs hosted: hosted is cheaper to start, dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation. we'll provide estimates both ways in the pricing doc.
[04:34] Aisha Rahman: for benchmarks, can you include hallucination detection metrics? like factuality score or binary hallucination flags?
[04:40] Ethan Kim: yes, we'll run automated hallucination heuristics and some manual spot checks; also recommend a small human eval panel for domain correctness.
[04:48] Dr. Lena Ortiz: success criteria for us: 1) factual accuracy at least 95% on key clinical facts (blood values, med names) in spot checks; 2) p50 latency under 400ms for 200 token outputs for interactive; 3) throughput to handle 40 concurrent requests with batching during batch windows; 4) multilingual quality acceptable for spanish/french (qualitative pass by PM).
[05:14] Ethan Kim: that's clear — we'll encode that into the benchmark plan. any specific privacy checklist items?
[05:18] Priya Singh: we need KMS integration, SAML SSO, audit logs retention 1 year, and the ability to redact PII on ingestion for the POC.
[05:28] Sofia Patel: noted. we'll include those in the security pack.
[05:31] Markus Chen: about model selection — you mentioned LoRA. can we iterate on LoRA in the POC? how long does a light domain adapt take?
[05:38] Ethan Kim: small LoRA on 1-10k examples can be done in days on a few GPUs; it's optional but useful if out-of-the-box models aren't hitting accuracy. we'll propose runs for both zero-shot and LoRA + retrieval variants.
[05:50] Dr. Lena Ortiz: are there licensing concerns with LLaMA-3 or others for our use-case?
[05:54] Sofia Patel: we'll flag IP/licensing for each open model in the security doc; some have restrictions, we'll summarize.
[05:59] Aisha Rahman: for reporting, can you include cost per request estimates based on quantized execution?
[06:04] Ethan Kim: yes, we'll provide cost per 1k tokens and per inference for each model/config, including 4-bit and 8-bit quantized runs.
[06:11] Sofia Patel: quick recap and actions: Biovanta to send sample dataset (anonymized 5k rows) and success criteria doc. Redwood (Ethan) to run baseline on Mistral-7B, LLaMA-3-13B, Falcon-40B-instruct, MPT-30B including quantized variants and produce p50/p95 latency, throughput, GPU util, and quality metrics. Sofia to send pricing, pilot SOW, and security pack. schedule deep-dive on VPC/KMS after initial data handoff.
[06:36] Dr. Lena Ortiz: sounds good, timeline ok. we'll aim to provide the dataset by end of tomorrow.
[06:42] Priya Singh: i'll coordinate the security contacts and review SOC docs once received.
[06:47] Sofia Patel: thanks everyone. we'll follow up over email with the artifacts and propose times for the deep-dive.
[06:53] Ethan Kim: thanks all, talk soon.
[06:55] [call ends]
